title: PQT canonical dataset manifest, schema version 2
description: Describes one build of an exported research dataset. The backend generates it; a consumer validates against this schema before reading a single row. The two languages agreeing on a file is what keeps them from drifting apart, which ADR-004 raised and left open.

dataset_id.description: Derived from the export parameters, not issued at random, so the same request names the same dataset.

dataset_version.description: Which build of this dataset it is. Deliberately excluded from content_hash.

schema_version.description: Which manifest shape this is. A reader that does not know the version must refuse rather than guess which fields it can trust.

content_hash.description: Digest over every field except dataset_version, created_at_utc and created_by_commit — the three that say which run this was rather than what the data is. Recompute it on load; a mismatch means the manifest's own fields were changed after the export.

known_as_of_utc.description: The observation instant the bars were read at, or null for the current series. Null is a legitimate export and a different object from a point-in-time one.

adjusted.description: Whether prices were rescaled for corporate actions.

announcement_policy.description: What the read did with an action whose announcement date is unknown. A dataset built permissively carries look-ahead into every experiment run against it.

universe_as_of.description: The date the constituent set was read at, for an as_of dataset; null for a point_in_time one, which reads membership on every session. Never later than to_date, or the export applies a later membership to earlier prices.

membership.description: How rows were matched to membership. as_of: one constituent set, read at universe_as_of, applied to the whole window. point_in_time: a row exists only where its instrument was a member that session, and each instrument lists its spells. See ADR-024.

instruments.description: The exported set. The identifier is the identity; the ticker is a label valid at universe_as_of, or at export time for a point_in_time dataset, and appears nowhere in the data rows, so nothing can be joined on it by accident.

spells.description: For a point_in_time dataset, when the instrument was a member within the window: from is inclusive, until is the exclusive date it left or null if it was still a member at to_date. announced_on is when the change was published; trading it earlier is look-ahead. Null for an as_of dataset.

interval.description: The bar resolution, in the spelling the API and the operator CLI accept.

transformation_version.description: Normalisation rules the bars passed through. A dataset that cannot say which rules produced it cannot be reproduced when those rules change.

sources.description: Every provider that contributed a row, with what this deployment records about its right to the data. A dataset that cannot say where its rows came from cannot answer whether it may be redistributed.

files.description: The data files. Hashes are verified on load, not merely recorded: a reproducible result computed from a silently changed input is worse than no result.

name.description: Relative to the dataset build's directory. Never a path.

row_count.description: Total rows across every file. Derived from files[].row_count and written for convenience; it is not part of content_hash because the file hashes it summarises already are.

created_by_commit.description: The build that produced the export, or null when the build recorded none. Null rather than a placeholder: a dataset claiming a commit it does not know is worse than one that admits it.
